assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a minimal stochastic model that organises a very large class of non-equilibrium growth and interface phenomena into one universality class, with exact solutions (Tracy-Widom statistics, integrability) and a clean experimental realisation in liquid-crystal turbulence. It is the kind of surprisingly universal, simply stated and rigorously analysable mechanism I value most, and it connects statistical mechanics to random matrices.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 equation; only Kardar and Zhang are in the credited names (Parisi already holds the 2021 prize, so this is not a barrier in principle). Takeuchi and Sano supplied the decisive experimental confirmation of the universal distributions. The exact-solution contributors (e.g. Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) are not credited, so the configuration is incomplete in terms of who established the mathematical picture.
assessment.maturity: The theory dates from 1986, the exact solutions from about 2010, and experiments (2010-2012 onward) are independent and quantitative. The interpretation is stable and the field is still active and extending to quantum systems, so recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees KPZ as sufficiently distinct from the 2021 complex-systems recognition and from Parisi's work.
The pivotal mathematical solutions are not in the credited list, and the experimental role of Takeuchi relative to the theory is a judgement call.
My recollection of exact priority details among exact-solution authors is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture proposes that loose, disordered packings of grains, foams and colloids undergo a rigidity transition with critical scaling, anchoring glassy and granular matter in a single phase-diagram concept. It is a conceptual unification of soft-matter systems with universal exponents, in the spirit of critical phenomena, and has been tested in simulations and experiments.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal of a jamming phase diagram is the originating idea; O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel's 2003 simulations established point-J criticality. Liu and Nagel are the natural pair; adding O'Hern would be a defensible third name but I judge the conceptual origin to lie with the two. Contributions by others such as Durian, Behringer and Wyart are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strong numerical and experimental support exists for the scaling near the isostatic point, but the upper critical dimension, the role of thermal fluctuations, and the exact universality class in real laboratory systems remain debated. It is mature in influence, but the status of the transition as a true critical point is still partly unsettled.
uncertainties: Whether jamming is a genuine thermodynamic-like critical phenomenon or a protocol-dependent crossover.
Experimental confirmation of critical exponents is less clean than in simulation.
Soft matter has little precedent at the Nobel level beyond liquid crystals and polymers; reception is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a new boson consistent with the Standard Model Higgs completed the electroweak sector and confirmed a half-century-old mechanism. The experimental achievement, combining detector design, trigger systems and statistical analysis at an unprecedented scale, is of the highest importance and has been followed by measurements of couplings and spin-parity.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theorists; the experimental side is a collaboration of thousands, and the credited list has four names but a prize allows at most three. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement), Jenni (ATLAS founder-spokesperson) and Virdee (CMS) are one possible selection; Della Negra's CMS founding role is equally strong, so the choice is arbitrary in part and exposes the difficulty of crediting large collaborations.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by two experiments is complete and later Run 2 and Run 3 data have confirmed couplings. Recognition is timely, with fourteen years since discovery.
uncertainties: Attribution inside ATLAS and CMS is inherently contested and a three-person limit cannot represent the collaborations.
Whether the committee wishes to honour a collaboration-scale discovery without a clear individual leadership signal.
Several measured Higgs couplings (self-coupling) remain unknown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states created a new field of tunable moire quantum matter. The pairing of a simple continuum theory with striking experiments, and the control of strong correlations by a single geometric parameter, is fresh and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 magic-angle prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental demonstrations. Credit for other contributions (e.g. Cao, Dean and Efetov experiments, Santos, Lopes dos Santos and Peres for early theory) is relevant and unresolved, and a prize here would have to address that.
assessment.maturity: The field is under eight years old at the time of the key experiments and the origin of the superconductivity is not settled. The existence of the flat bands and correlated states is well replicated, but the explanation for the pairing is not yet stable.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene remains disputed.
Possible premature recognition given the field's rapid evolution.
Credit among the early theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) is not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves the horizon and flatness problems and provides a quantum-fluctuation origin for primordial structure that is quantitatively tested by the CMB. It is a conceptually unifying idea linking quantum field theory to cosmological structure, and the generation of nearly scale-invariant fluctuations is a calculable and compelling mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario (1981), Linde (and Albrecht-Steinhardt) fixed the graceful exit via new inflation, and Mukhanov-Chibisov and Starobinsky derived the fluctuation spectrum. Starobinsky, Sato and others are missing from the credited names, and the allocation of priority among them is a well-known dispute that prevents a clean three-person division.
assessment.maturity: The predictions of near-scale invariance, Gaussianity and flatness are supported by WMAP and Planck, but the specific inflationary model is unconfirmed and primordial gravitational waves have not been detected. The Committee has historically wanted a more direct confirmation.
uncertainties: Absence of primordial B-mode detection leaves the mechanism indirectly supported.
Credit disputes with Starobinsky and others not listed.
Alternative explanations for the CMB patterns have not been excluded in a decisive way.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kane and Mele's prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect from spin-orbit coupling in graphene, together with its observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened the study of topological insulators in which a bulk band invariant guarantees protected edge states. It is a clean theory-to-experiment story and a major conceptual advance in condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the Z2 invariant and the 2005 prediction; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in 2007 following the proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. Because Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane are outside the credited names, the allocation is imperfect and the 2016 prize for topological phases partly overlaps with the subject.
assessment.maturity: Observation is robust and well replicated in many materials, and the theory is stable. Recognition is mature, but the 2016 Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz prize reduces the novelty of this area.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2016 topological-phase recognition.
Missing names (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu) whose contributions to the HgTe proposal were decisive.
Kane and Mele's original graphene prediction was later found to involve a very small gap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, allowing the observation of the superfluid-Mott transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and quantum gas microscopy of strongly correlated states. They offer a controlled testing ground for many-body theory that can be directly compared with analytical models, which I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch et al.) proposed the lattice Hubbard realisation, Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition (2002), and Esslinger achieved fermionic Mott insulators; credited names include four people and the selection of three leaves out Zoller's theoretical foundation. Greiner's quantum gas microscope work with Bloch is also decisive. The attribution is therefore truly split between proposal and demonstration.
assessment.maturity: The platform is widely replicated and mature, but the 2001 and 2012 prizes on condensates and trapped atoms already overlap partially, and the key target, simulating high-temperature superconductivity, is not yet reached.
uncertainties: Choice between proposing theorist Zoller and the experimental trio.
Overlap with previous cold-atom prizes.
Whether the simulation has yet delivered new physics beyond known models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory in two dimensions provides exact solutions for critical phenomena and underpins string theory, critical exponents and the classification of universality classes. The c-theorem and the use of conformal invariance for statistical models are central pillars of modern theoretical physics and of the modern understanding of universality, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: The foundational 1984 paper was by Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov; Belavin is not credited, and Cardy's contribution (finite-size scaling, modular invariance and boundary CFT) is separate. Friedan, Qiu and Shenker and Dotsenko-Fateev also made decisive contributions, so a three-person selection is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature and its predictions for critical exponents are confirmed in 2D systems, but the Nobel Committee generally requires direct experimental relevance; the connection is mostly to idealised statistical models and numerical checks, and recognition is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit omissions (Belavin, Friedan, Dotsenko, Fateev) and lack of a clean three-person split.
Limited direct experimental confirmation in actual physical systems, as most checks are numerical or in special 2D realisations.
The Committee's historical reluctance to reward formal theory.
